question: A 79-year-old man with a history of prostate cancer is brought to the emergency department because of lower abdominal pain for 1 hour. He has not urinated for 24 hours. Abdominal examination shows a palpable bladder that is tender to palpation. A pelvic ultrasound performed by the emergency department resident confirms the diagnosis of acute urinary retention. An attempt to perform transurethral catheterization is unsuccessful. A urology consultation is ordered and the urologist plans to attempt suprapubic catheterization. As the urologist is called to see a different emergency patient, she asks the emergency department resident to obtain informed consent for the procedure. The resident recalls a lecture about the different modes of catheterization, but he has never seen or performed a suprapubic catheterization himself. Which of the following statements by the emergency department resident is the most appropriate?

options.opa: “I will make sure the patient reads and signs the informed consent form.”
options.opb: “I would be happy to obtain informed consent on your behalf, but I'm not legally allowed to do so during my residency.”
options.opc: “Suprapubic catheterization is not the treatment of choice for this patient.”
options.opd: “I would prefer that you obtain informed consent when you become available again.”
options.ope: “I will ask the patient to waive informed consent because this is an urgent procedure.”

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Acute urinary retention" -> "Lower abdominal pain" -> "Not urinated for 24 hours" -> "Palpable tender bladder" -> "Pelvic ultrasound confirms acute urinary retention" -> "Unsuccessful transurethral catheterization" -> "Urologist plans suprapubic catheterization" -> "Emergency department resident to obtain informed consent" -> "Emergency department resident recalls lecture on catheterization" -> "Emergency department resident has not performed suprapubic catheterization" -> "Emergency department resident asks for guidance on obtaining informed consent" -> 80%
enhanced_information: Suprapubic catheterization is a valid option for acute urinary retention when transurethral catheterization fails. The emergency department resident should obtain informed consent for the procedure as requested by the urologist.
analysis: Suprapubic catheterization is a valid and appropriate option for acute urinary retention when transurethral catheterization fails. The emergency department resident should assist in obtaining informed consent for the procedure as requested by the urologist to ensure patient autonomy and understanding of the intervention.
